The Dragons felt like they had a great chance in Auckland. (Getty Images: Andy Jackson)

St George Illawarra captain Damien Cook has accused the NRL of favouring bigger teams after his side's narrow loss to the Warriors in Auckland.

The Warriors claimed a nervy 20-12 victory to stay within touching distance of the Panthers at the top of the NRL ladder.

However, Cook fumed over a number of refereeing decisions that he said went against his side, including a clear forward pass to Dallin Watene-Zelezniak that allowed him to score the go-ahead try just after half time.

The Warriors also earned two penalties in the closing stages, allowing Chanel Harris-Tavita to ice the game from the kicking tee.

"We're not getting rewarded for the effort we're putting in," Cook said in the post-match press conference.

"The Warriors got a lot of stuff out there, we're putting a lot of effort, we're fighting for play the balls, we're not getting the same six agains.

"We come out at half time, they throw a forward pass [and] we're chasing points straight away when we're in control of that game.

"It's not right."

The Warriors claimed victory over the Dragons, but it was not without controversy. (Getty Images: Andy Jackson)

The Dragons had a try disallowed when winger Setu Tu was ruled to have been tackled by Warriors fullback Taine Tuaupiki and held him.

Tu got up and ran to the line and scored, but Dean Young said the call was "a big turning point" and, had Tu been told to play the ball, the Dragons would likely have scored.

Cook suggested that the Dragons' lowly position on the NRL ladder influenced the refereeing decisions that went against his team.

"I feel sorry for the fans," he said.

"They have to watch that, but it's happening too many times to us.

"I don't know if it's because we're sitting down the bottom, it's an easy one to throw off because you know the Warriors should win today.

"So I think it's unfair and we deserve better moving forward."

In the opening game, the Raiders hung on to beat the South Sydney Rabbitohs 34-24 at Canberra stadium.

However, the win came at a cost for the Raiders, who lost Blues forward Hudson Young, who was carried from the field after going down with a non-contact, left lower leg injury, confirmed by the Raiders as being a suspected Achilles rupture.

Hudson Young was carried off with what was described as a ruptured Achilles tendon. (Getty Images: Mark Nolan)

The injury ends the Raiders star's season, ruling him out of the World Cup to boot.

"I feel for him personally," Raiders coach Ricky Stuart said.

"He is such a massive part of our team.

"It hasn't hit him yet, but he misses the rest of the season and misses the World Cup.

"I've been there personally and it hits you in the next couple of days, but he's got the right people around him."

That came after Melbourne conformed that winger Will Warbrick ruptured his Achilles tendon on Friday night and will undergo surgery early next week, ending his season and his Storm career.

In the late game, Canterbury-Bankstown thumped Wests Tigers 32-0 at Stadium Australia.

In the NRLW, the Roosters beat the Raiders 22-18, the Warriors crushed the Cowboys 42-4, and the Bulldogs beat the Sharks 24-18.

And fair enough, I reckon - the Warriors certainly did seem to get the rub of the green earlier tonight, scoring after what looked like a forward pass and earning a couple extremely soft late penalties.

Sat 18 Jul 2026 at 9:27pm

By Simon Smale

Canterbury Bankstown Bulldogs have dominated the Wests Tigers, scoring five tries to nil in a crushing 32-0 victory.

Sean O'Sullivan kicked a 40:20 in the opening set, Jethro Rinakama scored in the corner not long after, and the Bulldogs never looked back.

Josh Curran scored twice, with Enari Tuala and the brilliant Matt Burton also crossing to condemn the Wests Tigers to yet another season without finals football.

Latu Fainu and Alex Twal were both sin binned late on for the abject Wests Tigers, who were forced to play with just 11 men in the closing stages.

The Bulldogs excelled, with O'Sullivan impressive and Lachlan Galvin also controlling play with the ball in hand.

Their form showed that the Bulldogs, now just on the edge of the top eight, are still in the hunt for a finals spot.
